title: BTS Opens Debut El Paso Run — Night 1 at Sun Bowl Stadium; Surprise Songs 'ON' + 'OUTRO: WINGS [NEW]'
detail: On May 2, 2026, BTS performs the first of two sold-out nights at Sun Bowl Stadium on the UTEP campus in El Paso, Texas — the group's first-ever performances in El Paso and in the US–Mexico border region. The stadium's capacity of approximately 51,500 is sold out for both nights, with fans traveling from across West Texas, New Mexico, Houston, Dallas, Austin, and Ciudad Juárez, Mexico. Pre-show lines for official merchandise formed as early as 9 AM, with KTSM 9 News documenting ARMY taking over the downtown corridor and the Sun Bowl area ahead of the 8:00 PM showtime. The Night 1 surprise songs are 'ON' (from the 2020 album MAP OF THE SOUL: 7) and 'OUTRO: WINGS [NEW]' — a new arrangement of the 2016 Wings-era track, marking its debut performance. The ARIRANG World Tour rotating 360-degree stage fills the Sun Bowl end zone configuration, allowing viewing from all sides. El Paso Mayor Oscar Leeser and UTEP President Heather Wilson are reported to be in attendance. KVIA and KTSM both cover the fan community gathering ahead of the event, describing the cross-border ARMY presence as transformative for the city's hospitality economy. The El Paso run follows the Tampa, Florida leg (April 25–28, three nights, ~190,000 fans) and precedes a Las Vegas residency at Allegiant Stadium (May 23, 24, 27, 28).

title: South Korean Prosecutors Reject Police Arrest Warrant for HYBE Chairman Bang Si-hyuk; Police Weigh Re-Filing
detail: South Korean prosecutors reject a police request for an arrest warrant targeting HYBE Corporation chairman Bang Si-hyuk, citing insufficient evidence. The police had alleged investor fraud: that Bang misled early HYBE shareholders in 2019 ahead of the company's 2020 IPO, allegedly collecting approximately 30% of proceeds (roughly KRW 190 billion / $129 million) via a private equity side arrangement without disclosing it to co-investors. Prosecutors determined the case requires further investigation before an arrest threshold is met. Police are reportedly considering re-filing. Bang has publicly denied all wrongdoing. The case is separate from HYBE's ongoing operations: the ARIRANG World Tour is proceeding on schedule, HYBE's Q1 2026 earnings posted a record $478 million in revenue, and no change in Bang's executive role has been announced. The legal situation first drew international media coverage in late April 2026 via Variety, Deadline, and Korean broadcaster reporting. Analysts from NH Securities and Hanwha Investment maintain HYBE buy ratings, noting the legal proceedings are unlikely to materially affect the BTS comeback revenue arc through 2026–2027.
